This article describes Muku Shrine in Shimoyoshida, Chichibu, Saitama.

== Overview ==
Its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}} was prefectural shrine. It was originally called Ikura Gosho Daimyojin, and "Ikura Jinja" is considered the original reading. In the early modern period, people from outside the area increasingly read it as "Muku Jinja," which became the current name. {{ill|Ryusei Matsuri|ja|秩父吉田の龍勢|qid=Q11679207}}, where {{ill|Ryūsei (signal rocket)|Q11679206|qid=Q11679206}} are launched during the {{ill|Reisai|Q11385469|qid=Q11385469}}, is well known.

On October 31, Meiji 17 ({{ill|1884|Q7819|qid=Q7819}}), it was also the site of the uprising rally of the {{ill|Chichibu incident|Q3078148|qid=Q3078148|lt=Chichibu Konminto}}. In 2004, the 120th anniversary year of the Chichibu Incident, filming for the commemorative movie "{{ill|Kusa no ran|Q11618062|qid=Q11618062}}" was held here.

* {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|az|Sarutahiko|fa|ساروتاهیکو اوکامی|fr|Sarutahiko Ōkami|it|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|ko|사루타히코 오카미|mni|ꯁꯔꯨꯇꯍꯤꯀꯣ ꯑꯣꯀꯃꯤ|pl|Sarutahiko|ru|Сарутахико|simple|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ta|சருதாகிகோ அகாமி|tr|Sarutahiko Ōkami|zh|猿田彥|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto}}
*: During Yamato Takeru's eastern expedition, guided by a shining spear, Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto appeared from the shade of a muku tree by a well and guided the way. The spear was treated as the sacred object and Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto was enshrined.

'''Kami-Makita Muku Shrine'''
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Onamuchi-no-Mikoto}}
*: During Yamato Takeru's eastern expedition, guided by a shining spear, Onamuchi-no-Mikoto appeared from the shade of a muku tree by a well and guided the way. The spear was treated as the sacred object and Onamuchi-no-Mikoto was enshrined.

== Origin ==
According to shrine tradition, it was founded by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|lt=Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258}} during his eastern expedition.

The origin of the shrine building is said to be in {{ill|710|Q23518|qid=Q23518}} ({{ill|Wadō (era)|Q1373026|qid=Q1373026}} 3), when {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tajihi no Mahito}} dedicated five to of rice and labor service.

== Cultural properties ==
* Nationally designated Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property
** Chichibu Yoshida no Ryusei

** Muku Shrine main hall

** Suji kabuto (helmet)

== Access ==
'''Shimoyoshida Muku Shrine'''
* From {{ill|Chichibu Station|Q5096049|qid=Q5096049}} on {{ill|Chichibu Railway|Q843780|qid=Q843780}} or {{ill|Seibu-Chichibu Station|Q7446590|qid=Q7446590}} on the {{ill|Seibu Chichibu Line|Q842649|qid=Q842649}}, take {{ill|Seibu Kanko Bus|Q11628934|qid=Q11628934}} bound for "Yoshida Genkimura" (Chichibu Yoshida line). Get off at "Ryusei Kaikan" and walk 10 minutes.
*: Note: buses are infrequent.

'''Naka-Makita Muku Shrine'''
* From Chichibu Station or Seibu-Chichibu Station, take Seibu Kanko Bus bound for "Ogano Depot" or "Kurio." Get off at "Naka-Makita" stop.

'''Kami-Makita Muku Shrine'''
* From Chichibu Station or Seibu-Chichibu Station, take Seibu Kanko Bus bound for "Ogano Depot" or "Kurio." Get off at "Fusaka Iriguchi" stop.

== Location ==
